before:
The local declaration var asks the compiler to infer a fixed static type from its initializer; it is not a dynamically typed variable. filter keeps elements whose predicate is true; map transforms retained elements. Neither changes the source list. toList is a terminal operation that obtains the resulting list.

list.stream() takes no arguments and creates a sequential stream over that collection; it does not copy the list into a new result list.
For 1, 2, 3, 4, keeping even values leaves 2 and 4; multiplying each by ten produces 20 and 40. Stream.toList returns an unmodifiable list, not a promise about its concrete class.
Expected output or behavior: [20, 40]. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
Optional local transfer task: Predict map-before-filter using a predicate on the mapped values. You may trace it without a JDK; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: A stream describes steps for processing values from a source. stream() starts one from the list. filter keeps values that pass a true-or-false check, and map transforms those retained values. These operations do not change this source list.

Here, filter keeps even numbers using % to check the remainder after division by two. map then multiplies each kept number by ten. toList finishes the stream and collects its answers in a list that cannot be changed.
The program prints [20, 40]. Filtering keeps two and four, then mapping turns them into twenty and forty.
The quiz keeps odd numbers instead. The mapping step stays the same, so apply it to the newly selected values.
